candidates: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:57 - Ties at order 200 now resolve silently, so FIPS and non-FIPS providers can be mixed.. Before this change, finding more than one provider threw an error, which stopped a FIPS deployment from running with the non-FIPS provider. Now `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider` and `FIPS1402Provider` all return 200. The stable sort keeps them in ServiceLoader (classpath) order, and the first one wins with only a debug log. If both `keycloak-crypto-default` and `keycloak-crypto-fips1402` end up on the classpath (for example through a packaging mistake), a FIPS deployment can quietly run on plain BouncyCastle. Fix: keep throwing when the top two providers have the same order, so only a lower-priority fallback such as the authz-client provider is skipped silently.

common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java:44 - New abstract `order()` breaks every existing CryptoProvider implementation outside this change.. `CryptoProvider` is a public SPI in keycloak-common. Adding a method with no body means any custom or downstream implementation, including the copy in the keycloak-client repository this is meant to sync with and any test providers not shown here, stops compiling. Already-compiled ones throw `AbstractMethodError` when `detectProvider` sorts them. Make it `default int order() { return 0; }` (or some other neutral value) so existing implementations keep working.

authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:114 - Two unused ASN1Encoder instances are built and thrown away.. `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` build encoders whose results are never used. The encoders actually used are built again on lines 119-120. Delete these two lines.

authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:42 - Every ES test signs with the default P-256 key, so ES384 and ES512 are never tested with their real curves.. `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` uses the JDK default curve (P-256) for all three tests. For ES512, r and s are then only about 32 bytes, padded out to 66. The real P-521 case, where the integers are 66 bytes and the DER sequence needs a long-form length (more than 127 bytes), never reaches the new ASN1Encoder/ASN1Decoder code. Generate a key for each algorithm with `initialize(new ECGenParameterSpec("secp256r1"/"secp384r1"/"secp521r1"))`.
